candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: Kraken Robotics operating context now distinguishes KATFISH towing and topside processing, with August 27 results and Canadian delivery detail that help assess a supplier conversation. Evidence: 10 sources from Kraken Robotics and Canadian government buyers separate manufacturer specifications, reported finances and the RMDS contract amendment. Mission/Public Need read: Existing underwater ISR relationships remain unchanged; KATFISH towing and topside processing provide the concrete capability premise without creating a new demand match. Unknowns: The C$12,154,000.20 contract reduction is not explicitly connected to the C$1.5 million revenue reversal, and the XL-UUV customer remains unnamed. Reviewer action: Inspect the operating context and reviewed questions against W8472-105270/001/QF and the KATFISH fact sheet before accepting the proposed dossier.
reviewWarnings: The CanadaBuys C$12,154,000.20 reduction on W8472-105270/001/QF is not explicitly linked by the reviewed documents to Kraken's C$1.5 million Q2 revenue reversal; do not equate the two amounts or infer cancellation.
SeaPower brochure specifies 2 kWh minimum while the current product page says 1.8 kWh; confirm the offered module and certification package rather than treating the ranges as interchangeable.
The XL-UUV battery customer is unnamed, and announced orders, master supply agreements and management guidance do not establish delivered revenue or future production throughput.

organization.name: Kraken Robotics
organization.description: See the seabed and underwater objects in high resolution from a towable survey system. Kraken Robotics develops synthetic-aperture sonar, subsea imaging, power, and robotic technology from Canada.
organization.current_activity: On July 2, 2026, Kraken Robotics closed its approximately C$615 million acquisition of Covelya Group, adding Sonardyne, EIVA, Forcys, Voyis and Chelsea while establishing a broader Kraken Group governance structure.
organization.operating_context: Kraken Robotics is a St. John's marine-technology group developing synthetic-aperture sonar, subsea batteries and underwater sensing systems, with acquired specialist subsidiaries retained as distinct operating businesses. Its published capability portfolio includes Synthetic-aperture sonar and subsea energy systems.
organization.canadian_footprint: Kraken Robotics has a documented Canadian operating presence in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. Its public organization and capability evidence should be read at that location and national scope only where the cited sources explicitly support it.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: COVE operating context now identifies Stella Maris test requirements and DRDC experimentation roles, helping companies decide which access conversation to pursue. Unknowns: Project-specific funding and trial access remain conditional, while the historical Start-Up Yard intake is not confirmed open. Reviewer action: Review the operating context and September 2, 2026 current activity with the Communitech relationship, preserving the planned-event and intake limits.
reviewWarnings: The September 14–18 Waterloo Tech Week activity is planned; the September 2 collaboration does not establish completed adoption, funding or procurement outcomes.

Stella Maris funding is conditional and project-specific; published material does not give a tariff, confirmed slot, interface acceptance or classification/security approval for a particular deployment.
Sea Tracker is supplied by Ultra Maritime for DRDC experimentation; COVE collaboration does not establish ownership of the sonar product or unrestricted third-party access to defence trials.
The old Start-Up Yard program URL returns 404 and the current service index labels Incubators coming soon; verify current intake before routing a company to the historical participation record.
